message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you run | Where it goes |
|--------|--------------|---------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (requires the Cloud SDK) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/instances` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, etc.) |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS. In GCP the equivalent is a Compute Engine instance.*  
> *Make sure you have the **GPU** API enabled, a GPU quota for the zone you choose, and that billing is active.*

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to match your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports A6000 GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-a6000,count=1" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --service-account="default" \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What the flags do

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk (you can increase if you need more storage) |
| `--maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` | If the host machine is reclaimed, the VM is terminated (default is MIGRATE) |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a shell script at first boot |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules (if you want to expose services) |
| `--service-account` | Uses the default Compute Engine service account (or specify another) |
| `--scopes` | Grants the VM full Cloud Platform access (adjust if you need tighter scopes) |

> **Tip** – If you want a *pre‑emptible* instance (cheaper but can be stopped at any time), add `--preemptible`.

---

## 2. REST API (curl)

Below is a minimal JSON payload that you can POST to the Compute Engine API. Replace `<PROJECT>` and `<ZONE>` with your values.

```bash
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# JSON body – save to a file or use a here‑document
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API call (you need an OAuth 2.0 access token)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Explanation of the JSON

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type (`n1-standard-8`) |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, 100 GB SSD) |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Uses the default VPC and gives the instance an external IP |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access |
| `tags.items` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script (installs NVIDIA driver) |

> **Important** – The `acceleratorType` URL must match the zone you’re using. If you’re in a different zone, replace `$ZONE` accordingly.

---

## Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Enable GPU API**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Check GPU Quota**  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=$ZONE
   ```

3. **Billing** – Ensure your project has billing enabled.

4. **Permissions** – You need `roles/compute.admin` (or equivalent) on the project.

5. **GPU Driver** – The startup script above installs the NVIDIA driver. If you need a specific driver version, adjust the script.

---

### Done!  
Run the gcloud command or the curl POST, and you’ll have a Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy computing!
